target.title: fix(slack): read resolved userToken with env fallback in channel type resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveSlackConversationInfo()` uses `account.config.userToken` to resolve the token for Slack API calls. `account.config.userToken` only contains the raw config value — it does **not** include the `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` environment variable fallback.

Users who set `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` env var without also configuring `channels.slack.accounts.<id>.userToken` in the config file get an empty token, causing channel type resolution to silently fall back to `"unknown"` for non-DM channels.

## Changes

- `channel-type.ts:88`: `account.config.userToken` → `account.userToken`
- `account.userToken` is the resolved value that includes env fallback (`configUser ?? envUser`)

## Evidence

**Unit tests (7/7 passed):**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Lint:** `npx oxlint` — no errors

**Type check:** `pnpm tsgo` — no errors

**Real behaviour proof (hostname + timestamp + before/after):**
```
Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
PID: 130921
Time: 2026-07-10T06:23:22.511Z

=== Bug Reproduction: env-only userToken ===

Scenario: User sets SLACK_USER_TOKEN env var, no config userToken
Config value (account.config.userToken): undefined
Resolved value (account.userToken): "xoxp-...cdef"

--- Before fix (account.config.userToken) ---
  token = EMPTY ❌
  → channel type API call SKIPPED, always returns "unknown"

--- After fix (account.userToken) ---
  token = SET ✅
  → channel type API call PROCEEDS, returns correct type
```

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
